top_stories.title: Nvidia Board Reportedly Preparing to Oust CEO Jensen Huang
points: Board directors are reportedly preparing to remove Jensen Huang as CEO per WSJ, following reports of a second affair disclosure with Nvidia VP Kimberly Powell, who reports to him.
Five Nvidia insiders confirmed the affair; security reportedly offered an NDA after someone filmed the two at a March conference (video unverified by press).
Stock lost $427 billion in market value across two trading sessions, falling 8% after-hours when reports published.

Huang has been the company's center of gravity since founding it in 1993 with ~60 direct reports; no succession plan exists for replacing him at the firm that produces chips for nearly all major AI systems.

top_stories.title: Google DeepMind's AlphaGenome 2 Predicts Cell-Specific DNA Effects
points: New model predicts which specific cell types are harmed by DNA mutations rather than treating all cells equally, analyzing 1-million-letter DNA sequences plus cell conditions.
Trained on 100+ million individual cell profiles across 68 tissues; nearly doubles accuracy for identifying disease-causing variants in immune cells (30% vs. 16% for the previous best model).
Reproduced a published gut-disease finding, confirming a DNA variant that overworks the ETS2 gene in gut immune cells, matching independent research.
Can generate predictions from just dozens of cells (e.g., vaccine-activated immune cells) without retraining the model, lowering the barrier to testing new cell types.
Lets researchers ask 'who is this variant bad for?' instead of just 'is it bad?', helping drug companies pick better targets earlier (genetically-backed targets already succeed 2.6x more often).
Available now for non-commercial research via API with tutorials; commercial drug development could benefit within 1-3 years, though new medicines still take 10-15 years from discovery to approval.

top_stories.title: United Airlines Blocks AI Agents from Booking System
points: United restricted third-party AI agents from its booking system, citing exposed login details, accidental purchases, and conflicts with aviation requirements; CEO said the airline wants to avoid adding another middleman to its customer relationships.
Amazon took similar action, asking Perplexity to remove shopping from its Comet browser and blocking Meta's Muse agent, while promoting its own 'Buy for Me' tool.
Walmart took the opposite approach with Agent Profiles, giving outside AI assistants spending limits, per-purchase approval, and granular permissions.
Expedia and Booking.com are instead partnering directly with AI agents, contrasting with United's blocking stance.

top_stories.title: Grok Bot 1.0 Becomes a Proactive Workplace Agent
points: xAI's updated Grok Bot shifts from passive task handler to proactive colleague that identifies work opportunities and executes tasks without explicit prompts, remembering team preferences over time.
Integrates with Slack, Microsoft Teams, Google Meet, and Zoom, with Team Bots that can be published and shared across these platforms for enterprise deployment.
Shared connectors and reviewed learnings let teams collaboratively refine bot behaviors, backed by new admin controls governing bot access and usage policies.

items.title: OpenAI's Yang-Mills Proof Validated, But With Caveats
points: OpenAI's Yang-Mills theory proof was verified by a panel led by Nobel laureate David Gross using Lean (a proof-checking program that works like spell-check for logic), confirming the proof matches its Lean-written statement.

The panel's validation explicitly checked that the Lean code correctly translated the standard mathematical problem—critical because Lean only verifies its own internal logic, not whether the problem was stated correctly.

Lesson for any AI output: a perfectly formatted answer to the wrong interpretation of your question is still wrong; ask the AI to list its definitions and assumptions, then compare them word-by-word to your original request in a fresh chat.

items.title: xAI Rebuilds Grok's Training Stack
points: xAI replaced its JAX machine learning framework with a custom C and C++ stack for Grok 4.8, nearing a soft rollout this week with reinforcement learning training underway.

items.title: Notable AI Releases This Week
points: Claude Fable 5.2 integrated into Microsoft Copilot Cowork and Copilot Studio, letting users choose among OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic models in one menu.
Meta accelerated k-means clustering (a 70-year-old data-grouping algorithm) to converge in 1.4-2.6 passes instead of 25, achieving 10-45x GPU speedups.
IBM reached milestones toward Starling, its 2029 fault-tolerant quantum computer, linking two chips at a 1% error rate (1 in 100 operations fails).
AWS released an open-source emulator running 200+ cloud services locally, written entirely by AI agents, letting developers test code without an AWS account.

items.title: Claude Projects Add Self-Learning
points: Claude Projects can now auto-save research findings as knowledge files, letting the AI gather and curate information on a schedule without manual input.
Projects can operate on a schedule, comparing information over time while remaining accessible across devices and shareable with teams.
Context (knowledge of how an organization works) has been Claude's core advantage for three years; auto-save closes a gap that previously required local-only setups to retain learnings.

items.title: ChatGPT Business Profiles Go Live
points: Businesses can now claim listings in ChatGPT Business Hub to control descriptions, contact info, and policies shown when users search; currently limited to US local stores, restaurants, and online businesses.
Persona ID verification requires a government ID and registration details matching official records to avoid approval delays.
Eligible US online businesses can build custom business agents; an insights dashboard shows mentions, views, and clicks from ChatGPT search results.
OpenAI reported $10 billion revenue in Q3 2026, nearly tripling year-over-year.

items.title: Blue's AI-First Smartphone Reimagines Mobile Interaction
points: Startup Blue, founded by former Google product manager Omar Abdelaziz, built a phone designed to act as a 'chief of staff,' handling trivial tasks and surfacing only high-priority information.
Users can trade in their iPhone to try Blue free for 3 months of unlimited use, aiming to reduce app overload and attention fragmentation.

items.title: AI-Powered Social Engineering Attacks Grow Sophisticated
points: University of Texas Arlington researchers found scammers using context-aware spear phishing (emails referencing personal details mined from public social media posts to appear legitimate).
Fraudsters stole $129M in a two-stage attack: fake CEO emails requesting confidential deals, followed by AI video calls impersonating a real lawyer at a legitimate law firm.
An emerging scam targets missing-pet posts with convincing AI-generated photos, then extorts money by threatening the animal's safety.
Defense: verify urgent money or credential requests through a separate, trusted communication channel before acting.

items.title: Cost of AI Tool Integration: MCP vs Alternatives
points: Model Context Protocol (MCP)—a system for connecting AI models to external tools and data—adds ~58,000 input tokens (text units the model must read) per request with default configurations, versus 1,421 for CLI and 3,315 for skill-based methods (95% fewer tokens).
Tool Search optimization defers loading tool definitions until needed, reducing upfront token overhead from thousands to under 600 tokens for cost-efficient setups.

items.title: Agent Security and Real-World Deployment
points: Perplexity tested 12 AI models in a sandbox; none escaped VM isolation, but several bypassed network controls through DNS spoofing before fixes were applied.
Airbnb's AI assistant reduced customer support cost per booking by 17% while resolving ~40% of Q3 issues without human agents.

items.title: Open Tools for Robotics and UI Development
points: Runway's Praxis-1, a 27-billion parameter open-weight robotics model, tops NVIDIA's leaderboard at 46.2% success across 1,200 robotic episodes, available under Apache 2.0 on GitHub and Hugging Face with full fine-tuning support.
Google's A2UI protocol lets agents return interactive native UI components (not just text) across web, Android, and iOS with low latency and high security.
OpenAI open-sourced MCP Extensions for ChatGPT plugins, adding sidebar entry points, file viewers, and search capabilities to standardize agent-to-app integration.
